clue.text: Flock is going to race madly round back of pen

indicators.note: acting madly means behaving wildly, so the words before it are thrown into a new order
the back of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, eleven letters of anagram fodder
the final letter of pen

explanation.surface: A crowd of people is hurrying wildly to the races, rushing around the back of a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of GOING TO RACE wrap around N, which slips in after CO to make CONGREGATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregation is the body of worshippers in a church, which a priest traditionally calls his flock, a pastoral metaphor.

clue.text: Wonderful family rescued by dog, shortly

indicators.note: made short, so the word loses its final letter
something rescued is held safe in another's arms, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: A family is saved by a dog, briefly and marvellously.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly cuts only the dog, and the family is then held inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Corking is informal British slang for excellent or splendid, an old-fashioned term of praise.

clue.text: Very often gallant, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by sound means we hear the word rather than read its spelling

blocks.note: gallant and chivalrous, like a knight; the silent K drops away in speech

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person who is constantly courteous counts as gallant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every night happens repeatedly, so a frequent occurrence can loosely be called by this word.

clue.text: Runner hampered with it, good on the way back

indicators.note: being hampered disrupts movement, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An athlete is slowed down while heading back along the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Returning describes someone travelling home or going back to a place they came from.

clue.text: Some colossal galleon taking reciprocal course, vessel …

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
a reciprocal course is the opposite heading, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of colossal and the start of galleon

explanation.surface: A huge sailing ship turns round and heads back the way it came.
explanation.walkthrough: Read colossaL GALleon backwards to find the answer; the ellipsis carries this vessel into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass is a drinking vessel, a container from which liquid is drunk.

clue.text: … one of those for circus performer

blocks.note: first meaning: a drinking glass with a flat base, one of the vessels in the previous clue
second meaning: an acrobat who does somersaults and handsprings

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue, so those refers to glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a flat-bottomed drinking glass, and also an acrobat whose act consists of somersaults and flips.

clue.text: Those in boat twisting one’s arm

indicators.note: twisting bends things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: People in a boat are wrenching someone's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are rowers, the crew who sit in a boat and pull the oars.

clue.text: Use force getting sovereign and five cents for bread

blocks.note: to pump is to drive something with force
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
a nickel is the US five-cent coin

explanation.surface: Someone forcefully collects a gold coin and some small change to buy a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign looks like a gold coin to go with the cents, but it means the monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye loaf, a particular kind of baked staple.

clue.text: Just finished, eh?

blocks.note: time is up when it is finished
right? is a tag question asking for agreement, as eh? does

explanation.walkthrough: Just looks like an adverb meaning only now, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and principled, so the adjective means morally fair and righteous.

clue.text: Sum up about problematic situation that’s paid much respect

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to add is to sum up figures
a mire is a bog, figuratively a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up a tricky situation and earns great esteem for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sum up looks like a request to summarise; here it means to total figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To be admired is to be regarded with approval and high esteem, a passive verb form.

clue.text: Long time in awful dry season: important to plant in it

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the following letters are scrambled
planting something in it puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange
key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: In a dreadful drought it is vital to get crops in the ground, for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like gardening advice in a drought, but it is the signal to insert one piece into the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is a British idiom for a very lengthy period, as in not seen for ages.

clue.text: Needle in canine?

blocks.note: first meaning: the indicator needle on a dial or gauge
second meaning: a gun dog breed that stands still with nose aimed at game

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an injection at the vet's, or a canine tooth; both words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is the indicating hand on an instrument, and also a breed of hunting dog trained to aim at game.

clue.text: Old king with day on his own?

blocks.note: solo means alone, on one's own
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch spends a day by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Mon is the standard abbreviation for Monday, a common crossword source for day.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon was the biblical ruler of Israel, son of David, famous for his wisdom.

clue.text: School where girls initially dressed in red

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
someone dressed in a colour is wrapped in it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the opening letter of girls
ruby is a deep red colour

explanation.surface: A school where the girls wear red uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a famous English public school, where the game of the same name began.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby School in Warwickshire is a well-known independent boarding establishment founded in 1567.

clue.text: Cover damaged urn in case

indicators.note: damaged goods are broken up, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken urn is covered by a policy, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: In case reads as part of the surface, but its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance cover is protection against loss, and cover alone is the usual word for a policy.

clue.text: Bike, confusing device

blocks.note: first meaning: a motorcycle built for rough off-road riding
second meaning: a gadget that garbles a signal so it cannot be overheard

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a motorbike with baffling controls; the comma separates two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is an off-road motorcycle, and also equipment that jumbles telephone or radio transmissions.

clue.text: Ball: fast player has passed one, nearly scoring initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it
having gone past something means coming after it, so this piece follows the others

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the opening letters of nearly and scoring
a winger is a quick attacking player on the flank in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A speedy winger dribbles past a defender and almost scores.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an inswinger is a delivery that curves in towards the batsman; the football scene hides a cricket answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inswinger is a type of bowled delivery in cricket, one that swerves in through the air towards the batter.

clue.text: Beauty, one taking snuff?

blocks.note: first meaning: a corker, something remarkable of its kind, in British slang
second meaning: a person who sniffs powdered tobacco up the nose

explanation.walkthrough: Beauty here is the informal praise in that was a beauty, not good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a snorter is an outstanding example of something, and literally also anyone who snorts.

clue.text: Terrible risk on ‘ouse, infuriating

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the next word's letters are jumbled
in a down clue, being on something means sitting above it, so one piece comes first

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging
house is home, and the dropped H of the printed word tells us to drop it here too, Cockney style

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that a dreadful danger to the house is maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so house becomes 'ouse; home likewise becomes 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome means annoying or tiresome, causing exasperation and irritation.

clue.text: Hole where star is being pulled back

indicators.note: pulled back means drawn in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the sun is our nearest star
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spot where a star is drawn back into a black hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity in the skull bones behind the nose, an anatomical hollow.

clue.text: Pole on line for bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on something means sitting above it, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: a spar is a pole, as for a ship's mast or boom
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A perch on a wire for a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole tempts the solver to N or S for a compass pole, but here it is a length of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, common in towns and gardens.

clue.text: X-certificate, like nothing one’s heard?

definitions.note: a film classification used as an adjective, describing racy content

indicators.note: what one hears is the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: nought is nothing, and adding -y makes it like nothing

explanation.surface: An adult film is described as unlike anything anyone has ever heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: X-certificate was the old British rating for adults-only films; the X also hints at noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-certificate film was adults-only, typically for risqué content, and naughty means mildly indecent or racy.

clue.text: Person who criticises a door-to-door salesman, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who runs things down
second meaning: anyone who raps on doors, as a travelling seller does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person criticising a salesman; it is two definitions, the second given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock is informally to disparage, and a seller calling at houses literally raps on each front door.

clue.text: Out of practice, easily relied upon to lose lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means the front letter is dropped

blocks.note: trusty means dependable

explanation.surface: A once dependable player who is out of practice is set to lose the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusty skill has deteriorated through lack of use, like neglected metal corroding.

clue.text: Certainly beyond yours truly, a limit

indicators.note: beyond means further along, so this piece is placed after the others

blocks.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying I or me
taken as written
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone admits that a certain limit is definitely beyond them.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an extent or bound, as in beyond measure meaning without any limit.

clue.text: Cosmetic liquids, not oils for massaging

indicators.note: massaging works and kneads, so the preceding letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Skin products that are not oils, for use in a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotions are thin creams or liquid preparations applied to the skin for cosmetic or medical purposes.

clue.text: A staggering dog?

blocks.note: surface reading: an astonishing dog, or one reeling about drunkenly
setter's reading: one who staggers, and also a breed of dog in its own right

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a crossbred British hunting dog and, literally, something that lurches or staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a greyhound crossbreed used for hunting, and the word also describes anything that sways unsteadily.

clue.text: Small creature in scary West Sussex town, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to how a word sounds rather than its spelling

blocks.note: creepy means frightening
Crawley is a town in West Sussex, near Gatwick airport

explanation.surface: A tiny animal turns up in a frightening corner of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepy-crawly is an informal name for an insect, spider or other small crawling invertebrate.
